_label: Evidence archive: www.wikioccupy.org, the studio's Occupy wiki, in its chat logs and a painting (November 2011)

identified_by.content: Evidence archive: www.wikioccupy.org, the studio's Occupy wiki, in its chat logs and a painting (November 2011)

content: Three chat logs, a private message and a photograph, all of November 2011, that record the studio principal describing his work on a website for the Occupy movement, www.wikioccupy.org, in the language of art. The earliest of the documents is a private Facebook message of 2011-11-01, sent at 17:54:55 UTC by Facebook's clock, in which the studio principal thanked a person who had liked 'the WikiOccupy page that i created', wrote 'I am the creator and admin of www.wikioccupy.org', called the project 'The Global Wiki', described himself as 'one of the key persons of the OWSGlobalWikiWorkingGroup', and gave as his contact an address at the site's own domain under the name 'Art'; the message carries a link to the wiki's home page and is signed with his own name. It does not describe the site as art. What it adds is a date fixed by Facebook, nine days before the first of the logs, for his role as the site's creator and administrator and for his use of the name 'Art'. The logs are of an Internet Relay Chat channel of an Occupy Wall Street wiki project, #owswikifarm, in which the studio principal took part under the name 'Art', and in the log of 10 November also 'ArtLight'. In the log dated 2011-11-19, of a discussion he moderated, he wrote, in this order: 'i own www.wikioccupy.org www.wikioccupywallst.org www.wikioccupywallstreet.org www.wikioccupy.com and www.wikioccupywallstreet.com'; 'as you can see i was/am very enthusiastic about the wiki occupy idea'; and 'as an act of Art'. Later in the same log he wrote of the project, 'i mean, its not like thats the only Art project in my life'. He described the site as 'happening right now, and is continuing to happen', described Sun and Rain Works as 'an Art based entity' and 'my legal entity which is my " Art business "', and wrote that 'the domain is currently registered through : Sun and Rain Works'. In the log of 2011-11-10 he wrote that he had 'other Art that i make also' and called himself 'simply an American Contemporary Artist, with " Art Assistants "'. Art is a recurring subject in what he wrote: of the roughly seven hundred lines that are his across the three logs, some forty-five mention art or artists in their text, apart from the name he used. Among them are 'Im in it for the Art !'; 'I am an Artistic visionary who has been working on this stuff for many years now. I just didn't join the movement 2 months ago.'; and an anecdote about the Grateful Dead's choice of name, 'because of their avant garde Art, and the meaning of words', followed by 'i.e. its kinda edgey like www.wikioccupy.org'. The photograph, taken with the studio's camera phone at 07:42:37 on 2011-11-16, shows a painting on paper whose subject is the site's address: 'www.' lettered in blue across the top and 'WiKioccupy.org' lettered in black beneath it. The studio states, in 2026, that it made www.wikioccupy.org as a work of Metaconceptual Art and as its part in the Occupy Wall Street movement; that the idea of a website as a work of art came from its earlier site, www.wtfisart.com; that the studio principal went by the pseudonym 'Art' throughout this period; and that he talked about art extensively in the project's chats and meetings. The site ran on MediaWiki, as its archived pages show. What the logs and the photograph show on their own is set out below: that in November 2011 the studio principal, as 'Art', described his holding of the site's domains, and the project, as art, returned to the subject of art repeatedly, and had made a painting of the site's address.

referred_to_by.content: Evidence status. The logs are held as three rich-text files, 11-10-11WikiChat.rtf, 32,280 bytes, SHA-256 ca1f7fcceb4c1be172ed5d2d5fecf26d523785912e9e1193f45e2e8d0154b157; 11-19-11GlobalWikiChat.rtf, 70,274 bytes, SHA-256 ab3e8f66cf3b3a39d29e819efee06b26892906ce93e528a076fc9902ce02a30b; and AeonJaggoffChatwiki11-19-11.rtf, 3,793 bytes, SHA-256 79056e5c83f20a7216c362803534ea2869525d74f451ed2e538f93a787e7b79f. They are the studio's own saved copies of a conversation with other people, and their lines carry times but no dates; the dates are given by the file names. They are dated more firmly by a message the studio principal sent from his mailbox on 2012-11-12 at 19:43:53 Pacific time, under the subject 'Art Historical Archives', to a private correspondent, which carries the three files as attachments, byte-identical to the copies now held, and which bears a message identifier of the form the Windows Live Hotmail service issued at that time. The logs therefore existed, in their present form, by 2012-11-13 at 03:43 UTC. One further check is internal: the channel topic recorded at the head of the 19 November log announces a meeting on 'Wednesday Nov. 16', and 2011-11-16 was a Wednesday. The logs are not published, because nearly all of their text is other people's; their checksums are, so that the held files can later be shown to be unaltered. The message of 2011-11-01 is in the account data Facebook compiled and delivered on request on 2026-09-24, held as facebook-joechirum-2026-09-24-TZ87gGfq.zip, SHA-256 c978c3bd338a6a9a934d3aa05a81d2c298c49200bf7e4edc98b8329c02103097, in a thread file of 1,756 bytes, SHA-256 45be57affddbfaaa95fd244dbfc371872ab3634831d7017727c7bb2831c27be8; its date is the one Facebook's servers assigned. The photograph is the camera's original, a JPEG of 2,048 by 1,536 pixels with its Exif block intact, held as 1116110742.JPEG, 471,800 bytes, SHA-256 ca9930c7d37af9bb1e86299d5b1165f2f1523cf83af9c76f1e8e1a224fa39d7d, and is published here at /images/wikioccupy-painting-2011.jpg as a byte-identical copy, renamed for the web and not otherwise altered.

How the photograph is dated. The Exif block names the camera as an LG Electronics LG-VX8575 with firmware VX857V06, the camera phone that made the photograph of 2011-11-08 set out in the inscription photograph record, and gives DateTimeOriginal as 2011:11:16 07:42:37. The file name, 1116110742, is the phone's own naming from month, day, two-digit year, hour and minute, and gives the same minute. The file carries no GPS data. The same phone photographed other studio works in the same half-hour that morning, among them the painted postcard of 07:29 set out in the postcard record. The date is the file's own account and is not notarized, and it dates the photograph, not the painting's making; the painting existed by that morning. No title for the painting is recorded here, and whether it survives is not stated.

The site itself, as archived. The Internet Archive first reached www.wikioccupy.org on 2011-10-24, when the address redirected into the wiki; pages of the running wiki were captured on 2011-10-25, and its main page on 2011-10-31 at 01:35:40 UTC, at https://web.archive.org/web/20111031013540/http://www.wikioccupy.org/index.php?title=Main_Page . That page, last modified on 30 October 2011, is titled 'Wiki Occupy Home', names its software in its own header as MediaWiki 1.17.0, the software of Wikipedia, and describes the site as 'an unofficial collective wiki for all of the occupy groups meeting up across the United States', and gives as its contact an address at the site's own domain under the name 'Art', the name the studio principal used in the chat. On 2011-12-03 the address returned only the hosting provider's default page. As captured, the site presents itself as a wiki for the Occupy movement and does not describe itself as a work of art; the art framing is in the studio principal's words in the chat, not on the site.

What these establish, and what they do not. They establish that on 2011-11-01, by Facebook's clock, the studio principal called himself the creator and administrator of www.wikioccupy.org and used the name 'Art' in his contact address for it. They also establish that in November 2011, in a conversation with other people and at a date fixed by a message of 2012, the studio principal described his holding of the wikioccupy domains 'as an act of Art' and the project as one Art project among others in his life, that he placed the domain under his art business, and that by 2011-11-16 he had made a painting whose subject is the site's address. Three limits go with that. The name he used in the channel was 'Art', so some of his phrases can be read either way: 'Art's project' may mean the project of the person called Art, and 'happening' may be meant in the ordinary sense of taking place, although the studio used the word of its own work elsewhere, as the archived-websites record sets out for 'Art Market Reform is a happening'. The line 'as an act of Art' follows 'i was/am very enthusiastic about the wiki occupy idea' and is quoted in sequence so that the reader can judge what it refers to. And the logs do not name Metaconceptual Art or mention www.wtfisart.com, Sotheby's or the sale of 2009, so the connections the studio draws, to Metaconceptual Art and to www.wtfisart.com as the source of the idea of a website as art, rest on its own account, given in 2026. Two dated facts sit close to that account without proving it: the studio principal's earliest public use of the word metaconceptual, in a posting of 2011-11-28 set out in the record of the 2011-2012 postings, falls nine days after the log of 19 November; and www.wtfisart.com, the earlier website the studio names as the source of the idea, was registered by the studio on 2009-03-16, as the registrar's receipts show. What this record adds, independently of the studio's account, is that in 2011 the studio did describe a website it ran, and its holding of that website's names, as art. It bears on no date before 2011.

Redaction and scope. Only the studio principal's own words are quoted. The other participants in the channel, the network addresses the logs record, the person to whom the message of 2011-11-01 was sent, the contact address it gives, and the correspondent to whom the logs were sent in 2012 are not named or given, and nothing any of them wrote is reproduced. No endorsement of this collection, of Metaconceptual Art or of any claim here by any person in the channel, or by the Occupy movement, is implied. The domain names are given because they are the subject of the record; both principal domains have since lapsed.

representation._label: A painting of the address www.wikioccupy.org, photographed on 2011-11-16
